prerequisites: It is recommended that students have completed the first-year course Physics I.

learning_outcomes.text: That students have the ability to collect and interpret relevant data (usually within their area of study) to make judgments that include reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their area of study.
That students can transmit information, ideas, problems and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Ability for oral and written transmission of information adapted to the audience.
Ability to apply new technologies, including information and communication technologies.
Ability to manage information, handle and apply technical specifications and necessary legislation for engineering practice.
Basic knowledge of production and manufacturing systems.
Knowledge of the principles of machine and mechanism theory.
Knowledge and use of the principles of strength of materials.

syllabus_topics: Applications of friction and energy aspects
Mechanics in Engineering. Error detection techniques. Calculation precision.
SI unit system, associated ISO rules. Basic trigonometric relationships.
Sum and decomposition of forces in 2D and 3D problems.
BLOCK 2. Solid, structure and machine statics
TOPIC 3. Mechanical effect of forces on a solid. System of forces.
Mechanical effect of a force on a solid. Moment of a force.
Equivalent force systems; Reduction of force systems on a solid.
Equilibrium of rigid solid in three dimensions.
Specific methods for solid equilibrium with forces at two points; and at three points.
Calculation of the resultant of internal forces in a solid section.
TOPIC 5. Statics of mechanical systems: Structures and Machines.
Equilibrium systems formed by linking different solids.
Analysis of forces in Machines and Trusses.
BLOCK 3. First and second order moments
TOPIC 6. Center of gravity, of mass and centroids.
Center of gravity of a solid.
TOPIC 7. Moments of inertia of plane surfaces.
Second order moments or moments of inertia.
Products of inertia. Principal axes of inertia.
Introduction to applications of moments of inertia in the calculation of structural element resistance.
Second order mass moments. Moments of inertia with respect to an axis.
Introduction to principal axes and inertia ellipsoid.
BLOCK 4. Applications of friction and energy aspects
Friction in bearings, in threads and rolling resistance.
Impulsive motion and collisions between particles.
Resolution of particle statics exercises and moments of forces.
Exercises on reduction of force systems and solid statics.
Exercises on calculation of reactions and forces in mechanical systems.
In situ measurement and calculation of moments of inertia of the cross-section of a real composite beam.
Experimental verification of stiffness and strength of beam specimens subjected to bending, in relation to the moments of inertia of their cross-section.
teaching_methods: Exposition of theory and general examples

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and/or participation in presential activities
Theoretical concepts of the subject (Written test)
Completion of assignments, cases or practical exercises

assessment_rules: The final grade for the ordinary call consists of a written exam (80%), attendance/participation (5%), practical exercises (10%), and lab practices (5%). To apply these weights, the score on the written exam must be 4.50 points or higher. For extraordinary calls, the final grade is solely based on the written exam score. The course is passed or failed in its entirety.
